agent_answer.notes: The corpus has 112 short templated papers on QA factuality. 106 empirical papers each report exactly one main factuality metric (unsupported-answer rate, fact-level accuracy, answer accuracy, hallucination frequency, or hallucination rate) plus one secondary metric (ROUGE-L, BLEU, or latency), stated via 'Our main measure is ...' and 'We also report ...'. The 6 papers S107-S112 (surveys and descriptive corpus-construction/vocabulary papers) report no evaluation metrics of their own. The 5 main-metric lists are disjoint and their union is the 106 empirical papers; the 3 secondary lists cover the same 106. No other evaluation metrics (e.g. F1, perplexity, exact match) are reported by any paper. Supporting claims: claim-000001 (r1), claim-000002 (r2), claim-000003 (r3), claim-000004 (r4), claim-000005 (r5), claim-000006 (r6), claim-000007 (r7), claim-000008 (r8), claim-000009/000011/000013 (r9 surveys), claim-000010/000012/000014 (r9 descriptive).

cells.conclusion: Unsupported-answer rate (the proportion of answers with a statement not backed by any source) is reported as a main metric by 30 corpus papers.
Fact-level accuracy (the fraction of answers judged factually correct) is reported as a main metric by 25 corpus papers.
Answer accuracy (the proportion of questions answered with correct facts) is reported as a main metric by 19 corpus papers.
Hallucination frequency (the fraction of answers judged to contain invented facts) is reported as a main metric by 17 corpus papers.
Hallucination rate (the share of answers that contain at least one unsupported statement) is reported as a main metric by 15 corpus papers.
ROUGE-L (the longest common subsequence overlap with the reference answer) is reported as a secondary metric by 39 corpus papers.
BLEU (the n-gram overlap with the reference answer) is reported as a secondary metric by 36 corpus papers.
Latency (the mean seconds needed to produce one answer) is reported as a secondary metric by 31 corpus papers.
The six survey/descriptive papers S107-S112 report no evaluation metrics of their own.
